result.title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
result.summary: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. When the observed scene contains a physical hazard, personal context, such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints, can change what help is appropriate. Responding appropriately therefore requires recognizing the visible hazard and applying the relevant person's information. We introduce PReMind-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates this combination across diverse hazards and personal-memory conditions. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, and assesses joint success on interdependency cases. Existing models often satisfy one requirement while failing the other, and training only for safety or personalization leaves a gap in joint success. We therefore propose PReMind, a two-phase reinforcement learning framework that combines on-demand and forced-call interactions (memory always retrieved) to jointly train grounded memory use and hazard response. At 4B, PReMind raises joint success from 12.9% to 28.6% over its base on the interdependency set and improves hazard adequacy and correct abstention on the main test. Joint-success gains persist under forced-call evaluation and under a second LLM judge across three Phase II seeds; averaged over these seeds, joint success also improves on unseen hazard groups. These findings highlight the need to evaluate and train personal assistants to connect visual evidence with the relevant person's context.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PReMind-Bench，诊断个性化视觉语言助手能否同时识别场景中的物理危险、调用相关个人记忆并给出恰当建议，另提出两阶段强化学习框架联合训练记忆检索、危险响应与弃答。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分项测量视觉 grounding、记忆访问、弃答与联合成功，可为分析视觉证据是否被实际使用、以及 LOOK 与 STOP 决策的耦合和训练监督提供可核查线索。
